To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of cottonseeds meal to increase dietary CP from 14 to 17.6% increased milk production and milk fat concentration and that increasing CP above 17% did not increase milk production but did increase blood urea and milk NPN.
increasing dietary CP level from 13.9 to 17.6% by the use cottonseed meal was of benefit to cows consuming alfala-based diets in early lacation.

the addition of cottonseed meal increased dry matter intake and milk yield of dairy cows in the early lactation period, and that increasing the dietary protein level above 17.6% did not increase milk yield.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of increasing dietary protein levels on the productivity of cows in early lacta-tion and the efficiency with which the increased dietary protein is utilized by the animal.
determining the optimum level of CP in the diet for dairy cows during early lactation and the effect of increasing the level of CP on milk yield and composition.
the response of early-lactation dairy cows to increased dietary protein levels by additions of a high-quality protein source.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the response of dairy cows in the early stages of lactation to additions to their alfalfa-based diets of cottonseed meal, a source of high-quality protein, was positive up to a level of approximately 17.5 to 20% CP, after which the response to additional protein was minimal.
increasing dietary CP from 13.5 to 17.0% by additions of cotton seed meal to diets for dairy cows in early postpartum lactation is beneficial to milk yield.
increasing dietary CP above 15% by the use or cottonseed meal in early lactation is not beneficial to milk yield.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a diet of 17.5 to 18% CP with a protein degradability of.32 is adequate for early lactation dairy cows.
the dietary CP level of 17.5%, with 1.0% rumen undegradable protein, is optimal for cows in early lactination.
increasing dietary CP by the use of high protein by-products such as cottonseed meal is an efficient way to improve milk yield and milk protein concentration in the first 4 to 8 wk of lactation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the addition of cottonseed meal (CSM) to alfalfa-based diets can increase the CP content to levels that are beneficial in early lactation and that CSM can be a useful tool to improve the protein nutrition in early lactation.
increasing dietary CP above 18% is probably not beneficial for dairy cows.
the addition of cottonseed meal is an effective means of increasing dietary CP in early lactation and that the response of cows to the added CP is positive.
